open_points.subject: A17
open_points.text: a misspelt name still stops the start, as the item it was meant to set is then missing
open_points.question: Does a misspelt service-token variable stop the start when no correctly named service-token variable is present, or does Registry ignore it and make the otherwise valid start owner-only?
options: Ignore the unknown variable and start owner-only because none of the four recognised service tokens is present.
Treat the misspelling as a missing intended service token and stop the start.
Stop only when at least one other correctly named service token makes the recognised set partial.
open_points.default_guess: Ignore the unknown variable and start owner-only, following the explicit rules that unknown variables are ignored and no service tokens is a valid owner-only configuration.

witness.initial: Every required non-service item is valid, and no correctly named service-token variable is present.
events: The owner sets only `REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKENN`, intending it to be PresuPro's token.
Registry starts and evaluates the configuration.
outcomes: `REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKENN` names no declared item, so Registry ignores it; the recognised service-token set is empty and Registry starts owner-only.
The misspelt token means the intended PresuPro item is missing, so Registry stops and names that item as missing.
witness.observer: The owner, who either receives a working owner-only Registry or a failed start diagnostic.

open_points.subject: A17
open_points.text: Registry reads exactly the items below and no other variable: a variable whose name names none of them
open_points.question: What exact environment-variable name denotes each listed item, and how are the four service names converted into variable names?
options: Declare an exact environment-variable name for every item.
Define one deterministic naming rule that covers every item and service token.
Leave the names to the implementation or deployment.
open_points.default_guess: Declare explicit uppercase names under the `REGISTRY_` prefix for every item, including a separately declared name for each service token.

witness.initial: The owner has valid values for the store location, backup location, backup key, owner credential and four service tokens.
events: One implementation looks for `REGISTRY_STORE`; another looks for `REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION`.
The owner supplies `REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION` and starts Registry.
outcomes: The first implementation ignores `REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION` and reports the store location missing.
The second implementation reads it and continues the start checks.

open_points.subject: A17
open_points.question: Now that `config` includes unknown `REGISTRY_` variables which are deliberately not checked, does `checks_passed(config)` mean that checks passed for the declared items only, or that every member of `config` was checked?
options: Define `checks_passed(config)` over only the projection of declared configuration items.
Redefine `config` to contain only declared items, leaving unknown environment variables outside it.
Require every `REGISTRY_` variable to be checked, which conflicts with the new rule and test.
open_points.default_guess: Define `checks_passed(config)` as successful completion of the ordered checks over recognised, declared items only.

witness.initial: All declared items are valid and the environment also contains `REGISTRY_EXTRA`.
events: Registry begins serving as Required test 7 requires.
outcomes: The invariant holds because `checks_passed` concerns only recognised items and ignores `REGISTRY_EXTRA`.
The invariant is false because `REGISTRY_EXTRA` belongs to `config` but was never checked; an implementation enforcing the invariant may therefore refuse the start.
witness.observer: The factory invariant check and the owner observing whether Registry serves.

open_points.subject: A17
open_points.text:
The configuration is a set of environment variables whose names begin
   with `REGISTRY_`, set as R0-23 says. Registry reads exactly the items
   below and no other variable:
open_points.rule: Таблица выше — исчерпывающий список путей значения, и у каждого из них своя форма: перечисление называется адресом, константа поставщика — `the imported X constant`, настройка — полем объекта настроек.
open_points.question: Replace the direct environment-variable path with named fields of the settings object, leaving environment access to the settings module.

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.kind: security review reopened but not reperformed
open_points.text: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
open_points.question: After the new A17 change made since the latest security review, is A21 currently reopened, and what new review result covers the categories that reference A17?
options: Reperform authentication_credential_abuse and secrets for the new A17 behavior and record the result before marking the review PERFORMED.
Mark the review reopened and pending until that review occurs.
Treat the existing 2026-11-11 review as covering a change that the round says occurred after it.
open_points.default_guess: Reopen A21, review authentication_credential_abuse and secrets against the new ignored-variable and misspelling behavior, and record a new result.

witness.initial: A21 is recorded as PERFORMED, and its authentication_credential_abuse and secrets categories reference A17.
events: A17 is changed after its latest review so that unknown `REGISTRY_` variables are ignored.
The design proceeds toward later states without adding another A21 review record.
outcomes: Under A21 rule 2 the security review is reopened and cannot remain complete until the affected categories are reviewed again.
If the old PERFORMED record is treated as sufficient, the design proceeds with no review of the changed configuration behavior.
witness.observer: The security reviewer and any release gate relying on A21's PERFORMED status.
